skill.name: npm-release
skill.description: Guides maintainers through a controlled cc-devflow npm release, including version synchronization, changelog updates, Git tagging, registry publishing, and verification.
skill.summary: Prepare, publish, verify, and recover cc-devflow npm releases.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed documentation references, authentication checks, and multilingual prose. The workflow does direct agents to run state-changing Git and npm commands, including publishing and destructive rollback, so explicit per-action approval is required. No prompt injection or obfuscated payload was found.

remediation.issue: Remote release commands can push Git state and publish an npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation immediately before each push and publish action, showing the exact branch, tag, version, package, and registry.

remediation.issue: Rollback instructions can unpublish a package, delete a remote tag, and revert a commit.
remediation.suggestion: Add a separate confirmation gate before every destructive rollback action and prefer a corrective patch after publication.

remediation.issue: The post-publish smoke test automatically executes the registry package with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Run the smoke test in an isolated temporary environment after verifying package integrity and receiving user approval.

content.value_statement: Manual npm releases can leave package files, tags, Git history, and registry versions inconsistent. This skill coordinates validation, versioning, changelog updates, publishing, rollback, and post-release checks.
actual_capabilities: Checks the worktree, target branch, unpushed commits, current version, and npm registry identity before release preparation.
Guides patch, minor, or major version selection and synchronizes package.json, package-lock.json, and CHANGELOG.md.
Runs repository publication verification and npm package dry-run checks.
Creates a structured release commit and annotated Git tag for the selected version.
Pushes the approved branch and tag, publishes the package, and verifies the registry version.
Documents recovery steps for failed pushes, failed publication, and critical post-publication defects.
limitations: The workflow is tailored to the cc-devflow package, repository structure, scripts, and changelog link.
It requires valid Git remote permissions and npm credentials for the target registry.
It performs high-impact Git and npm actions and must not run unattended.
It depends on a sibling repository skill that may not exist in standalone installations.

use_cases.title: Prepare a maintenance release
use_cases.description: Validate a clean branch, choose a patch version, update release files, and produce a reviewable commit and tag.

use_cases.title: Publish an approved release
use_cases.description: Run dry checks, push the approved branch and tag, publish to npm, and verify registry parity.

use_cases.title: Recover a failed release
use_cases.description: Assess local, remote, and registry state after failure, then select a controlled retry or rollback path.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a patch release
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a patch release for cc-devflow. Inspect the repository, show the proposed version and changelog changes, and stop before pushing or publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants reviewable local release preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a release candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a minor release from the current approved branch. Run dry checks, create the release commit and tag, then request confirmation before network actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer wants a validated release candidate.

prompt_templates.title: Audit version parity
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this release candidate for version parity across package files, changelog, commit, tag, and npm registry. Report blockers without changing state.
prompt_templates.scenario: A release manager needs an independent consistency check.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a failed publication
prompt_templates.prompt: Recover from this failed release: [paste error]. Determine registry, Git, and local state, propose the least destructive recovery, and wait for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced operator must reconcile a partial release.

output_examples.input: Prepare a patch release, but do not push or publish.
output_examples.output: Release preparation completed for version 1.1.1. Package files and changelog agree, verification passed, and the local commit and tag await approval.

output_examples.input: Check whether version 1.2.0 was published consistently.
output_examples.output: Registry verification passed. The package files, changelog, release commit, annotated tag, and npm registry all report version 1.2.0.

output_examples.input: The npm publish step failed after the tag was pushed.
output_examples.output: Publication is incomplete. Keep the existing commit and tag, record the registry error, verify authentication, and request approval before retrying publication.

best_practices: Confirm the exact worktree, branch, package, version, and registry before changing release state.
Require explicit approval immediately before remote pushes, publication, package execution, unpublish, or tag deletion.
Preserve failed release evidence and reconcile every package, changelog, commit, tag, and registry version.
anti_patterns: Do not release from a dirty or unapproved branch.
Do not skip npm identity checks, repository verification, or publication dry-runs.
Do not unpublish packages or delete tags to conceal a failed release.

faq.question: Which package does this skill release?
faq.answer: It is specifically configured for the cc-devflow npm package and its repository conventions.

faq.question: Can it choose the version automatically?
faq.answer: It explains patch, minor, and major choices, but the maintainer should approve the final version.

faq.question: Does it publish without confirmation?
faq.answer: The workflow contains real publish commands. Users should require explicit confirmation immediately before every remote or registry change.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The operator needs permission to push the target Git branch and tag, plus valid npm credentials for the configured registry.

faq.question: How does it verify a release?
faq.answer: It compares package files, changelog, commit, tag, and registry version, then runs package and help smoke checks.

faq.question: What happens after a failed publish?
faq.answer: It preserves the local commit and tag, records the registry error, and supports a controlled retry or approved rollback.
